In this work, we propose an accountability model for task-oriented conversations to mitigate user overreliance. Our approach aims to enhance the prediction of DST by detecting and correcting false positive and false negative errors, thereby ensuring greater accountability.

DST is primarily evaluated using joint goal accuracy (JGA). Additionally, we report the Slot-F1 score, false positive rate (FPR) and false negative rate (FNR).

DST is primarily evaluated using joint goal accuracy (JGA). JGA is defined as the percentage of turns where the predicted dialogue state exactly matches the ground-truth. Additionally, we report the Slot-F1 score, which measures the slot-level F1 performance.

We employ "GPT-4o mini" as our user simulator, assuming cooperative user behavior. Given the dialogue history and a slot-value pair (detected as false negative or false positive), the user simulator is asked to confirm if it mentioned the slot-value pair by responding "Agree" (confirms interest) or "Disagree" (rejects).
